issues.description: Class name mismatch with PR title: implemented as AWSAgentCoreProcessor but PR title says AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'Initial implementation of AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor' but the class is defined as 'AWSAgentCoreProcessor'. This is exported via 'from .agent_core import *' so the public API name needs to be locked in. Either rename the class to match the title, or update the title — but the discrepancy needs resolution before merge because renaming after release is breaking.

issues.description: Wildcard re-export via 'from .agent_core import *' has no __all__ defined
issues.detail: agent_core.py defines no __all__, so 'from .agent_core import *' leaks every public symbol including asyncio, json, os, aioboto3, logger, LLMContext, OpenAILLMContext, Frame, etc. into the aws package namespace. This pollutes the public surface and creates a brittle API where reorganizing imports later becomes a breaking change. Define __all__ = ['AWSAgentCoreProcessor', 'default_context_to_payload_transformer', 'default_response_to_output_transformer'].

issues.description: agentArn parameter name violates PEP 8 (camelCase in a Python public API)
issues.detail: The constructor parameter is 'agentArn' (camelCase) while the rest of the API uses snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region, etc.). This is a public API parameter — fixing it after release is a breaking change. Rename to agent_arn now. The internal attribute self._agentArn has the same problem.

issues.description: Default transformer drops assistant turn history — single-turn only
issues.detail: default_context_to_payload_transformer only forwards a payload when the *last* message has role 'user' or 'system' and otherwise returns None. This means after the first agent response is added to the context (role 'assistant'), the next user turn still works, but the entire conversation history beyond the latest single message is discarded — the payload is just {'prompt': '<latest text>'}. For an agent processor that takes an LLMContext, callers will reasonably expect multi-turn context to be preserved or at least configurable. Document this loudly as a limitation, or pass a richer payload.

issues.description: New aioboto3 client created per invocation — significant per-request overhead
issues.detail: Every LLMContextFrame opens a new 'async with self._aws_session.client("bedrock-agentcore", ...)' block, which performs credential resolution, endpoint discovery, and TLS setup on each call. For a streaming voice-agent pipeline this adds latency to every turn. Hold the client (or at least the context manager) for the lifetime of the processor, opened in setup() and closed in cleanup().

issues.description: No exception handling around AgentCore invocation or response parsing
issues.detail: client.invoke_agent_runtime and the async-for over response['response'] can raise (ClientError, network errors, decode errors). json.loads in default_response_to_output_transformer can raise on malformed input. Any of these will propagate up and crash the pipeline — and worse, will leave _output_response_open == True with the pending _close_task. Catch errors, log, ensure an LLMFullResponseEndFrame is pushed if a Start was already emitted, and consider an ErrorFrame.

issues.description: Timeout-based output response close is racy and unreliable
issues.detail: The processor uses a 1.0s sleep task to bookend LLMFullResponseStart/EndFrame. But process_frame already runs to completion before returning, and at the end (line 252-256) it cancels the timer and pushes the End frame explicitly. So the timer is effectively dead code for the normal path — yet the code still schedules it after every text frame inside the loop, creating churn. Either rely on the synchronous end-of-stream close (simpler and correct), or actually need the timer because text frames arrive asynchronously. The current design is confused.

issues.description: asyncio.get_event_loop() is deprecated outside a running loop and the value is unused
issues.detail: Line 174 assigns self._last_text_frame_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time() but the attribute is never read anywhere. Either remove it or use the value (and prefer asyncio.get_running_loop()). Dead state on a public processor is a maintenance hazard.

issues.description: SSE parsing is naive — splits on '\n' inside a part, but SSE events can be split across parts
issues.detail: The streaming branch decodes each part and splits on '\n'. SSE responses are not guaranteed to deliver a complete line within a single part — a line could be split across two parts (e.g., '{"resp' in one part and 'onse":"hi"}\n' in the next). The current code would log a warning and drop the data. Buffer trailing partial lines between parts, or use a streaming SSE parser.

issues.description: Major aioboto3 version bump (15.0 -> 15.5) without justification or compatibility note
issues.detail: The PR bumps aioboto3 to ~=15.5.0 and ripples botocore 1.38 -> 1.40 and boto3 1.38 -> 1.40 in uv.lock. ~= pinning to 15.5.0 means existing installs may need to re-resolve. No PR description explains why 15.5 is required (presumably the bedrock-agentcore client surface). State the minimum required version and why, and consider whether ~=15.0 with a >=15.5 floor would be less disruptive.

issues.description: Environment variable fallbacks read at __init__ time inside the processor
issues.detail: Most pipecat AWS services let aioboto3/botocore handle credential resolution via the default credential chain. Reading os.getenv('AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID') and explicitly passing it to the client overrides that chain unconditionally — bypassing IAM role assumption, SSO, ECS task roles, etc. Pass only what the caller explicitly supplied; let boto3 handle the rest.

issues.description: Default transformer asymmetry — input transformer returns Optional[str], output transformer can throw
issues.detail: default_response_to_output_transformer calls json.loads with no try/except. If the line is not JSON (which is plausible from a third-party agent), the whole process_frame crashes. The default input transformer is defensive; the default output transformer should be too — return None on parse error and log.

issues.description: No unit tests for transformers or process_frame branching
issues.detail: The transformers have clear input/output contracts and the SSE vs single-part branching is testable without AWS. Shipping a public processor without tests for at least the default transformers and the parse paths leaves regressions undetectable.

issues.description: Magic literal 'data: ' prefix and length 6 — easy to mis-edit
issues.detail: line[6:] hardcodes the prefix length. Define DATA_PREFIX = 'data: ' and use len(DATA_PREFIX). Minor, but the kind of nit that breaks once someone tries to support 'event:' lines too.

issues.description: Mixed import style: PEP 604 union 'LLMContext | OpenAILLMContext' alongside typing.Optional
issues.detail: Lines 22 and 121 use PEP 604 unions while the rest of the file uses Optional[X]. Pick one (Optional/Union or PEP 604) for consistency, and verify the project's minimum Python version supports PEP 604 at runtime (3.10+) not just in annotations.

issues.description: Docstring says input transformer handles 'system message if it's the latest' but says 'user or system' equivalently
issues.detail: Minor docstring/code drift — the docstring on the class explains 'Grabs the latest user or system message (if it's the latest message)' which is redundant phrasing. Clarify that any message other than user/system as the latest message yields no invocation.

dissents.topic: Whether to hold the boto3 client across invocations

positions.position: First iteration; per-call client is simpler and AWS clients are cheap-ish. Ship it, optimize later if profiling shows latency.

Voice pipelines are latency-sensitive by design. Setting up a fresh aioboto3 client per turn adds 10s-100s of ms and is exactly the kind of regression the framework should not bake in as default. Fix before merge.
AWS APIs use camelCase ('agentRuntimeArn'); mirroring that in the kwarg name reduces the impedance mismatch for AWS-fluent callers.
Every other parameter in this constructor and adjacent processors is snake_case. Inconsistency is worse than mirroring AWS, and renaming post-release is breaking. Use agent_arn.

dissents.topic: Bookending output frames with an asyncio timer

positions.position: The timer protects against future async paths where text frames arrive after process_frame returns; cheap insurance.

process_frame is fully synchronous w.r.t. the response stream — the explicit close at line 252-256 makes the timer dead weight that adds task-creation churn per frame. Remove it; rely on the synchronous end.

dissents.topic: Default transformer behavior — single message vs full history

positions.position: AgentCore agents typically take a single prompt; the default is the right minimal default and advanced users can supply a transformer.
An LLMContext encodes a conversation; silently throwing away all but the last message is surprising. At minimum, log a warning the first time, and document the limitation prominently.

review.summary: This PR adds a new AWSAgentCoreProcessor for invoking Bedrock AgentCore agents, plus a routine aioboto3 minor-version bump. The core flow is reasonable but several issues should block merge: the class name does not match the PR title, the module is wildcard-exported with no __all__ (leaking helpers into the public namespace), and the constructor uses camelCase 'agentArn' which is a breaking API mistake to ship. Beyond the naming concerns, the implementation has real correctness and performance gaps — a fresh aioboto3 client per turn, no error handling around invocation or JSON parsing, a confused timer-based response bookending scheme with dead state, and naive SSE parsing that can drop data split across response parts. Default transformer behavior (silently single-turn) needs to be at least documented loudly. Tests are absent. Fix the public API and error/lifecycle handling before merge; SSE buffering and client reuse can follow shortly after.
